passage: Few mistakes in reasoning are as common as the tendency to throw good money after bad. Economists call it the sunk cost fallacy: the belief that past investments justify future commitments, even when the future looks dim. A factory that has spent millions developing a doomed product will often keep pouring resources into it, simply because so much has already been invested. The same logic infects everyday life: people sit through bad films because they paid for the ticket, stay in unproductive relationships because of the years already invested, and persist in failing careers because turning back would feel like an admission of defeat. Rational decision-making, by contrast, requires evaluating each new choice on its own merits, asking not what has been spent but what is still to gain. The hardest lesson in economics, then, may also be the hardest lesson in life.

raw.direction: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
raw.explanation: 이 문장은 매몰 비용의 오류(sunk cost fallacy)와 대비(by contrast)되는 합리적 의사결정의 핵심 원리를 정의하는 핵심 문장이다. 필자는 앞에서 이미 투자한 것을 기준으로 미래를 결정하는 오류를 비판하고, 바로 이어 'asking not what has been spent but what is still to gain'이라는 구절로 빈칸의 내용을 부연 설명한다. 즉, 빈칸에는 과거 투자와 무관하게 '각 선택 자체의 장단점(merits)'만으로 판단해야 한다는 내용이 와야 한다. ①은 '누적된 총 비용을 따진다'는 뜻으로 오히려 매몰 비용의 오류와 동일한 사고를 반영한다. ②는 '과거 결정을 재검토한다'는 것으로 합리적 방향성처럼 보이나, 과거 실패에 초점을 두므로 'not what has been spent'라는 지문의 논리와 충돌한다. ④는 '과거 투자에 기반해 미래 약속을 최소화한다'는 뜻으로 여전히 과거 투자를 판단 기준으로 삼아 매몰 비용의 오류 범주에 속한다. ⑤는 '이미 투입된 자원을 고려한다'는 뜻으로 매몰 비용을 고려하는 행동 자체에 해당하여 정반대 개념이다.
keyPoints: 'by contrast'는 앞 내용(sunk cost fallacy)과의 명확한 대조를 신호하므로, 빈칸은 매몰 비용 오류와 반대되는 개념이어야 함을 파악해야 한다.

processed.passageWithMarkers: Few mistakes in reasoning are as common as the tendency to throw good money after bad. Economists call it the sunk cost fallacy: the belief that past investments __(a) justify__ future commitments, even when the future looks dim. A factory that has spent millions developing a doomed product will often keep __(b) pouring__ resources into it, simply because so much has already been invested. The same logic infects everyday life: people sit through bad films because they paid for the ticket, stay in unproductive relationships because of the years already invested, and __(c) persist__ in failing careers because turning back would feel like an __(e) admission__ of defeat. wrongOptionExplanations.5: (A)-(B)-(C) 순서는 (A)의 'The same logic' 지시 대상이 주어진 문장의 개념 정의뿐이어서 (C)의 공장 사례가 필요 없어지고, (B)의 결론이 중간에 위치한 뒤 (C)의 공장 사례가 덧붙여지는 구조가 되어 논증의 귀납적 전개가 깨진다.

processed.passageWithUnderline: Few mistakes in reasoning are as common as the tendency to throw good money after bad. Economists call it the sunk cost fallacy: the belief that past investments justify future commitments, even when the future looks dim. A factory that has spent millions developing a doomed product will often keep pouring resources into __it__, simply because so much has already been invested. The same logic infects everyday life: people sit through bad films because they paid for the ticket, stay in unproductive relationships because of the years already invested, and persist in failing careers because turning back would feel like an admission of defeat. Rational decision-making, by contrast, requires evaluating each new choice on its own merits, asking not what has been spent but what is still to gain. The hardest lesson in economics, then, may also be the hardest lesson in life.

sentences: Economists call it the sunk cost fallacy: the belief that past investments justify future commitments, even when the future looks dim.
A factory that has spent millions developing a doomed product will often keep pouring resources into it, simply because so much has already been invested.
Measuring the true return on investment requires accounting for opportunity costs, not just the capital already deployed.

The same logic infects everyday life: people sit through bad films because they paid for the ticket, stay in unproductive relationships because of the years already invested, and persist in failing careers because turning back would feel like an admission of defeat.
Rational decision-making, by contrast, requires evaluating each new choice on its own merits, asking not what has been spent but what is still to gain.

'requires' 뒤에는 동명사 'evaluating'이 목적어로 오고, 그 뒤에 분사구문 'asking not what has been spent but what is still to gain'이 이어져 합리적 의사결정의 방식을 구체화한다. 'not ~ but ~' 구문은 '지출된 것'과 '여전히 얻을 것'을 대조시켜 매몰비용 오류와 합리적 판단의 차이를 언어적으로 구현하며, 'what is still to gain'은 'be to 부정사'의 가능·예정 용법을 활용한 구조로 단순 미래나 조동사로 대체하면 오답이 된다. 또한 'by contrast'의 삽입 위치와 'on its own merits'라는 숙어적 표현도 정확히 재현해야 하므로, 단순 암기나 직역으로는 완전한 정답 도출이 어렵다.
keyPoints: 'requires + 동명사' 구문: 동사 'require'는 목적어로 동명사를 취하며, 여기서 'evaluating each new choice on its own merits'가 동명사구 목적어로 기능한다.
'not A but B' 대조 구문: 'not what has been spent but what is still to gain'처럼 명사절 두 개를 대조시키는 고급 구문으로, 매몰비용(과거)과 미래 이익의 대비를 문법적으로 표현한다.

Economists call it the sunk cost fallacy: the belief that past investments justify future commitments, even when the future looks dim. A factory that has spent millions developing a doomed product will often keep pouring resources into it, simply because so much has already been invested.
